I'm 45, finished middle school, and I've farmed here in Quzhou all my life. My family has about 8 mu of flat irrigated land, and I also help my brother run his small combine when the harvest rush comes. This year I'm keeping my main 6 mu in the wheat–maize rotation, same as always. The winter wheat went in last October and is greening up now; come early June I'll harvest it and put in summer maize no-till the same week. That two-crop system is the backbone around here—it's reliable, the grain buyers come right to the village, and I know how to manage it without hiring help. On the other 2 mu I'm planting cotton in April. Cotton means better cash than maize, but it also means spraying every ten days or so for bollworm and pruning by hand. At my age I can still handle 2 mu, but any more and I'd need labor I can't afford. For the wheat I'll run the rotary tiller once in early spring, topdress with compound fertilizer from the co-op, and irrigate four times—green-up, jointing, booting, and grain-filling. I'll spray for aphids and powdery mildew about four times. For the maize I'll buy Denghai hybrid seed, one package per mu, and plant straight after wheat harvest without plowing. I'll put compound fertilizer down with the seed and topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high, irrigate twice—tasseling and grain-fill—and spray three times for corn borer and weeds. The cotton gets rotary tilled, Guoxinmian improved seed, a potassium-heavy compound fertilizer, three irrigations, and twelve pesticide sprays through the season. If the weather cooperates I expect about 1000 jin per mu of wheat, 1200 jin of maize, and 500 jin of cotton.
